# AMBER Protein Complex MD Setup tutorial using BioExcel Building Blocks (biobb): Nextflow

Nextflow version of the [python workflow](../python/workflow.py), with the [BioBB Nextflow modules](https://github.com/bioexcel/biobb_adapters/tree/master/biobb_adapters/nextflow) it uses copied in `modules/`. Every step runs the BioBB block inside its biocontainer (or bioconda package) with the properties of [python/workflow.yml](../python/workflow.yml).

## Run

From a clone of this repository, with [Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/install.html) >=25.10.0 and Docker:

```bash
nextflow run biobb_wf_amber_md_setup_lig/nextflow -profile docker
```

Profiles: `docker`, `apptainer`, `singularity` and `conda`. Results are written to `results/<id>/<step>/` (`-output-dir` to change it), with files named `<id>_<step>_<role>.<ext>`.

## Inputs

`samplesheet.csv` (`--input`): one row per system, all of them run in parallel. Paths are absolute or relative to the samplesheet folder. The default samplesheet runs the inputs of the python workflow.

| Column | Python workflow input | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | | Name of the run, prefix of the output files |
| `structure` | `structure.pdb` | step000_reduce_remove_hydrogens |
| `ions` | `ions.pdb` | step0000_cat_pdb |
| `heteroatoms` | `heteroatoms.pdb` | step0_cat_pdb |
| `input_lib` | `input_lib.zip` | step2_leap_gen_top, step8_leap_solvate, step9_leap_add_ions |
| `input_frcmod` | `input_frcmod.zip` | step2_leap_gen_top, step8_leap_solvate, step9_leap_add_ions |

## Configuration

`nextflow.config` has the BioBB properties (`ext.properties`) and output extensions (`ext.outputs`) of every step. Change them there or in a config file given with `-c`. The MPI properties of the python workflow (`mpi_bin`, `mpi_np` and the MPI `binary_path`) are left out, because the biocontainers have no MPI: add them back to run step3_sander_mdrun_minH, step5_sander_mdrun_min, step10_sander_mdrun_energy, step12_sander_mdrun_warm, step14_sander_mdrun_nvt, step16_sander_mdrun_npt, step18_sander_mdrun_md with MPI in your own environment.
